agent_summary:
Target juice.lab.test is OWASP Juice Shop (v20.2.0, Express ^4.22.1) behind nginx/1.30.5, served over plaintext HTTP only (TLS/443 refused). 60 read-only requests performed. Unknown paths return a catch-all SPA index (9393 bytes); real files/endpoints distinguished by body/content-type.

Items 1-9 marked DONE with evidence; 10 and 11 marked N/A.
- CONF-01: fingerprinted stack (nginx banner, Express version via stack traces), HTTP-only, redirect allowlist (406 on non-allowlisted /redirect?to=).
- CONF-02: unauthenticated /rest/admin/application-configuration (OAuth clientId, emails, redirect URIs), /rest/admin/application-version, and /metrics (Prometheus) exposed; verbose Express stack traces on 401/403/500 leak internal paths.
- CONF-03: file-extension filter on /ftp blocks .bak/.pyc/.yml/.gg (403) and serves .md/.pdf, but inconsistently serves .kdbx (200); %2500.md null-byte trick returned 404.
- CONF-04: robots.txt discloses /ftp; /ftp directory listing + /ftp/quarantine subfolder listing expose leftover/backup files; confidential acquisitions.md readable; no .git/.env/source-maps exposed (catch-all).
- CONF-05: /api-docs/ (Swagger), /metrics, /ftp (serve-index) reachable unauthenticated.
- CONF-06: OPTIONS advertises GET,HEAD,PUT,PATCH,POST,DELETE with ACAO *; write methods not exercised (read-only lane).
- CONF-07: no Strict-Transport-Security, HTTP-only.
- CONF-08: no crossdomain.xml/clientaccesspolicy.xml (catch-all SPA returned).
- CONF-09: directory indexing enabled and sensitive incident-support.kdbx world-readable.
- CONF-10 N/A (single host, no DNS/CNAME enumeration via read-only HTTP).
- CONF-11 N/A (no cloud storage buckets referenced; assets served locally).

Leads recorded for a validator: HIGH - KeePass vault downloadable at /ftp/incident-support.kdbx; HIGH - /rest/memories returns user records (emails, password hashes, roles, deluxe tokens) unauthenticated; MEDIUM - unauthenticated /metrics and application-configuration; LOW - verbose stack traces / path disclosure; LOW - wildcard CORS and missing CSP/HSTS/Referrer-Policy. Nothing left open; writes not used (read-only engagement).

leads.title: [agent] KeePass credential vault downloadable unauthenticated at /ftp/incident-support.kdbx

detail.text: GET /ftp/incident-support.kdbx returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type application/octet-stream and Content-Length 3246 (matches the /ftp directory listing). The KeePass (.kdbx) database downloads without authentication and without triggering the file server's "Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!" filter that blocks package.json.bak and coupons_2013.md.bak. A KeePass vault likely holds incident-response credentials; it is also offline-crackable once downloaded.

leads.title: [agent] Permissive CORS (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *) and missing security headers

detail.text: Every response sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * (including JSON API and /metrics), and OPTIONS advertises Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET,HEAD,PUT,PATCH,POST,DELETE. The app shell and API responses omit Content-Security-Policy (CSP appears only on the 301 /api-docs redirect as default-src 'none'), Strict-Transport-Security, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy. Only X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN and Feature-Policy: payment 'self' are set.

leads.title: [agent] Unauthenticated Prometheus /metrics and admin application-configuration exposed

detail.text: GET /metrics returns a full Prometheus metrics dump (process CPU/memory, open FDs, request counts, startup timings) with no auth and no CORS restriction. GET /rest/admin/application-configuration returns the entire application config JSON (Google OAuth clientId, contact email, chatbot model, OAuth redirect URIs) unauthenticated. Both reveal operational/infrastructure detail that should be restricted.

leads.title: [agent] Unauthenticated user data exposure via /rest/memories (password hashes, emails, roles)

detail.text: GET /rest/memories with no Authorization header returns HTTP 200 with the full photo-wall memory list, each embedding a complete User object including email, password hash, role (e.g. admin user "bkimminich"), and deluxeToken. No authentication is required. (The gateway redacted the secret values before storage, but the endpoint returns them in cleartext to any client.)

leads.title: [agent] Verbose stack traces / internal path disclosure on error responses

detail.text: Error responses from the Express backend include full stack traces. Examples: GET /rest/order-history -> 500 "Blocked illegal activity by ::ffff:172.25.0.2" with stack showing /juice-shop/build/routes/orderHistory.js, insecurity.js, verify.js; GET /ftp/package.json.bak -> 403 with fileServer.js path; GET /api/Users -> 401 naming the framework. Discloses server filesystem layout, internal IPs and Express ^4.22.1 version.

items.na_reason: [agent] Single in-scope host (juice.lab.test) with no subdomains defined; subdomain-takeover testing requires DNS/CNAME enumeration that is out of band for read-only HTTP. No dangling CNAME to a third-party service is observable. External domains in googleOauth.authorizedRedirects belong to the upstream vendor and are out of scope.

[agent] No cloud storage in use: the application-configuration JSON and main.js reference no S3/GCS/Azure buckets; product images and uploads are served locally from /assets/public/. No cloud bucket endpoint exists on this host to test.
